svg.text: BCBC 2024 · DIVISION B · PART 9 HOUSING AND SMALL BUILDINGS · SECTION 9.23 WOOD-FRAME CONSTRUCTION
Lintel Spans and Sizes

g.text: At least 50 mm deeper than the tables show,

svg.text: WHAT THE CODE REQUIRES
Spans and sizes of wood lintels conform to the
spans shown in Span Tables 9.23.4.2.-L and
(a) for buildings of residential occupancy, (b)
where the wall studs exceed 38 mm by 64 mm in
size, (c) where the spans of supported joists do
not exceed 4.9 m, and (d) where the spans of
trusses do not exceed 9.8 m.
In loadbearing exterior and interior walls of
38 mm by 64 mm framing members, lintels
consist of
(a) 64 mm thick members on edge, or (b) 38 mm
thick and 19 mm thick members fastened together
with a double row of nails not less than 63 mm
long and spaced not more than 450 mm apart.
Lintels referred to in Sentence (2)
(a) are not less than 50 mm greater in depth than
those shown in Span Tables 9.23.4.2.-L and
9.23.12.3.-A to 9.23.12.3.-D for the maximum
spans shown, and (b) do not exceed 2.24 m in
length.
Drawn: 38 × 64 walls, upper part, lintels in yellow, A and B cut through the lintel. C: D is the table depth (red dashed). Sizes are illustration only.
Source: BCBC 2024, Division B, Article 9.23.12.3. (page 9-188)
